bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: North American large Ag continued softness; global economic slowdown; geopolitical tensions; tariff volatility; rupee appreciation reversing FX benefits
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and strategic; emphasizes operational resilience, dual-shore advantage, disciplined capital allocation, and inorganic growth pipeline; tone is upbeat on construction and European Ag, cautious on NA large Ag
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Mexico warehouse commissioning (Oct 2025) is a hidden catalyst for tariff mitigation and customer retention; 25% flat tariff on tractor parts (Oct 31) is a positive inflection for US aftermarket, not yet priced in
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- 'Our net cash position at the end of Q1 stands at INR 190 crore, reflecting the continued strength of our cash generation'; 'Our balance sheet is in excellent health'.
- 'When we declared the special dividend of INR 101cr in October 2025, our cash balance was approximately INR 210 crore. In ten months, through focussed operations and business growth, we have rebuilt to that level.'
- Debt/Equity has risen steadily but stays low: 0.02x FY23, 0.07x FY24, 0.09x FY25, 0.11x FY26.
- Returns on a trailing twelve-month basis per management: 'our EPS stands at INR 39.97, and our ROCE is north of 27%, with ROE at 20%'.
- Cash Flow from Operations has declined each year on the deck's own chart: INR 2,527 Mn FY23, 1,997 Mn FY24, 1,820 Mn FY25, 1,736 Mn FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- scale: Largest global share in tractor three point linkages and the lead position in precision machined parts for construction, forestry and mining equipment — evidence: the AR says it holds the top share of the global three point linkage market and leads the worldwide CFM precision machined parts space, with shares of 16.68% and 5.92% as of fiscal 2022 (the share figures are four years old)
- customer lock-in: Long-standing supplier to the largest OHV OEMs — evidence: it supplies all of the world's top ten off-highway vehicle manufacturers in agriculture and half of the top ten in construction (outside China), forestry and mining, and its top three customers have been with the Company for more than fifteen years
- distribution: Warehouse-led delivery close to customers in its export markets — evidence: three warehouses (two in the US, one in Germany), and 51% of FY2025-26 revenue came from warehousing sales (26% direct exports, 23% local deliveries)
- integration: Vertically integrated dual-shore manufacturing — evidence: six plants in India and one in the United States, each equipped for forging, machining, heat treatment, welding, surface finishing, prototyping and testing
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration — A significant share of revenue comes from a few key customers in the agriculture and CFM segments. The Company says relationships of more than fifteen years and its product and customer diversification reduce this risk.
- Macroeconomic and trade-policy risk (US tariffs) — Trade-policy uncertainty after the 2025 US tariff actions affects global supply chains and demand and remains a key concern. The Company monitors customer demand and keeps diversified sourcing and supply chains.
- Demand cyclicality in off-highway vehicles — OHV demand swings with agricultural conditions, commodity cycles and global infrastructure spending. The Company cites its diversified portfolio, dual-shore manufacturing and warehouse-based delivery as buffers.
- Currency risk — The Indian rupee fell 9.9% in FY2025-26. This makes exports more competitive but raises import costs. The Company manages the exposure through natural hedging and financial instruments as appropriate.
- Multi-jurisdiction regulatory and compliance risk — Environmental, labour and financial rules across several geographies keep changing. The Company relies on its governance framework and internal audit to find and fix compliance gaps.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Construction: 40-45% of revenue, green (strong growth from US AI infra & EU green energy); Large Ag: 17-20%, red in NA (soft), amber in EU (recovering); Small Ag: ~25%, green in Asia/India (GST cut boost), amber in NA (bottoming); Aftermarket: single-digit growth, subdued in EU (inventory), improving in US post-Oct 31 tariff ruling

business.body:
- 'Market leaders in small tractor (<70 HP) linkage system globally' and 'Leading global supplier in fragmented market with manufacturing base in India and US and servicing all major geographies (Americas, Europe, Japan, India, ROW)'.
- 'Servicing all 10 leading Global OHV OEMs in Agriculture and half of the leading 10 players in the CFM Segment' (footnoted as 'CFM global players outside China').
- Moat framed around product character: 'Complex, critical, and low volume high SKUs products'; 'Involved from the design stage for new products and launches providing end-to-end solutions'; 'Preferred component supplier for manufacturer of <70 HP Tractors'.
- Relationship depth: 'Four of the Top Five Customers have been Associated with Uniparts for over 10 years'; '~45% staff members working with Uniparts Group for 10+ years'; '250+ Engineers / Technical Diploma holders' and a '50+ strong Business Development and Sales / Customer Service organization'.
- Market size cited on the 3PL/PMP slide as '$1 billion+'.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order book] 'Our trailing twelve-month new business order book remains robust at over INR 225 crore, with a healthy pipeline. These wins span segments and geographies... The new business momentum is structural, and we intend to build on it.'
- [Customer concentration] The concentration chart reads top customer 28% / 27% / 31%, top 5 customers 61% / 64% / 71%, top 10 customers 76% / 78% / 84% across FY25 / FY26 / Q1FY27 - i.e. concentration stepping up in Q1FY27.
- [End markets] Construction equipment momentum from H2 CY2025 continues, supported by US technology-investment-led and European government-led infrastructure spending; large agriculture 'remains subdued', with leading OEMs indicating 'CY2026 represents the cyclical bottom, with a more meaningful recovery expected through CY2027'; western small ag is turning after 'three consecutive years of volume declines'.
- [Tariffs] 'Tariff-driven price volatility has led to some demand skewing, as higher prices caused customers and channel partners to moderate their purchasing. With tariffs having since come down, we expect this to normalise and the segment to return to growth.'
- [Certification] Milestones cite '3 units SER certified by Caterpillar' (2024) and 'Two factories SER certified by Caterpiller second year in a row' (2025); the covering exchange letter describes the company as 'An ISO 9001:2008 & 14001:2004 Company'.
- [Group structure] Uniparts India Ltd. sits above Gripwel Fasteners Pvt. Ltd. (GFPL), Gripwel Conag Pvt. Ltd. (GCPL), Uniparts USA Ltd. (UUL), Uniparts India GmbH (UIG) and Uniparts Olsen Inc (UOI); only two 100% holdings are marked and the extract does not bind them to specific entities.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Established in 1994, Uniparts India makes engineered systems and components for original equipment manufacturers and aftermarket clients in the off-highway vehicle, agricultural machinery and construction equipment industries. Its products are three point linkage assemblies, precision machined components, hydraulic cylinders, power take off devices and fabricated parts, made in six plants in India and one in the United States that do forging, machining, heat treatment, welding, surface finishing, prototyping and testing. It supplies customers through direct exports, local deliveries and warehouses in the US and Germany. About 85% of FY2025-26 revenue came from OEM customers and about 15% from the aftermarket.

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.200cr annualized new business awards over past 12 months; construction and European Ag driving new wins
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into hydraulics, large fabrications, PTOs via inorganic acquisitions; untapped potential in oil & gas, industrial machinery, mining (under construction segment); Asia and Europe as key growth corridors
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Three priority growth areas: large agriculture, construction and small to mid-size fabrication, chosen because they fit long-term market opportunities and existing manufacturing capabilities.
- Scale the Ludhiana fabrication facility, which currently contributes about one per cent of revenue and is expected to rise as order conversion improves.
- Inorganic growth: actively evaluating acquisitions in large fabrication, hydraulic and power take-off segments to broaden the portfolio, deepen customer relationships and expand markets, with stated capital-allocation discipline.
- After the US tariffs on imports from India, the precision machined parts portfolio and supply chain were realigned around best-cost-country sourcing product by product, with production of tariff-affected products moved to alternative locations, including US facilities.
- Pricing adjustments and cost pass-through mechanisms agreed with customers to protect profitability under tariffs.
- A dedicated cross-functional governance team tracks milestones on every new business programme to manage execution risk in the new business pipeline.
- Globally integrated manufacturing footprint that lets production move to the most efficient and resilient location.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Uniparts expands capacity through a modular model. It adds balancing equipment instead of building large greenfield plants and says it has enough manufacturing headroom to take on new business without significant upfront capital. Growth capex has been kept at 2.5-3.5% of revenue and goes to productivity, process optimisation and selective capacity additions. Utilisation is monitored plant by plant to remove bottlenecks. The footprint is seven manufacturing facilities (six in India, one in the US), with warehouses in the US, Europe and Mexico. In FY2025-26 the Company introduced lights-out manufacturing at its US facility and brought a critical manufacturing process in-house there. Surface finishing facilities are being upgraded at selected plants. The Farmparts facility in Ludhiana and the Vizag facility won industry cluster awards.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- FY2026-27 growth is expected to be broadly in line with the previous year, supported by a gradual recovery in industry demand, execution of recently secured business wins and improvement across end markets.
- North America construction equipment: continued growth expected through the coming year, with the second half outperforming the first; demand is driven by data centre build-out, reshoring of advanced manufacturing, digital infrastructure and Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act funds.
- Europe construction equipment appears past its cyclical trough, with the first signs of recovery in the last quarter; modest, genuine growth is expected in the year ahead, underpinned by infrastructure-led public investment, fiscal stimulus and energy transition projects.
- Small agriculture: North America is entering a recovery phase as farmers return to replacement cycles, with industry estimates of about five per cent growth; Europe is stabilising, with recovery expected to gather pace in the second half; India tractor demand has been stable. Management expects healthy growth in small agriculture.
- Large agriculture is still in a cyclical downturn: North American large tractor volumes are declining in the mid-to-high teens year on year, industry volumes are expected to fall a further fifteen to twenty per cent, and recovery will be gradual. Europe shows more encouraging signals.
- The aftermarket gives stable revenue in North America and Europe, largely insulated from swings in the original equipment cycle.
- West Asia tensions in March 2026 disrupted supply chains; the resulting rise in input costs was partly offset by favourable currency movements.
- Trailing twelve-month new business wins have crossed ₹225 crore (printed as 'H225 crore') and grew by more than twelve and a half per cent quarter on quarter; the wins are spread across several business lines and markets.
- In the small agriculture customer base, inventory replenishment is gaining momentum and order books continue to strengthen.
- New programme wins in Europe and participation across multiple tractor platforms position the company for the eventual recovery in large agriculture.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Uniparts delivered 14.6% YoY revenue growth and 22.6% EBITDA margin driven by rupee depreciation and Mexico warehouse commissioning, with construction and European Ag outperforming North American Ag; the normalized margin is 18-20%, and FY27 growth is expected to accelerate as markets recover.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Uniparts India is a dual-shore (India and US) maker of engineered systems for global off-highway vehicle OEMs, holding the top share of the global three point linkage market for tractors.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Established in 1994, Uniparts India makes engineered systems and components for original equipment manufacturers and aftermarket clients in the off-highway vehicle, agricultural machinery and construction equipment industries. Its products are three point linkage assemblies, precision machined components, hydraulic cylinders, power take off devices and fabricated parts, made in six plants in India and one in the United States that do forging, machining, heat treatment, welding, surface finishing, prototyping and testing. It supplies customers through direct exports, local deliveries and warehouses in the US and Germany. About 85% of FY2025-26 revenue came from OEM customers and about 15% from the aftermarket.

end_markets.body:
- Agriculture (tractors; manufacture of agricultural and forestry machinery parts, NIC 28219)

growth_optionality.body: Expansion into hydraulics, large fabrications, PTOs via inorganic acquisitions; untapped potential in oil & gas, industrial machinery, mining (under construction segment); Asia and Europe as key growth corridors

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- FY2026-27 growth is expected to be broadly in line with the previous year, supported by a gradual recovery in industry demand, execution of recently secured business wins and improvement across end markets.
- North America construction equipment: continued growth expected through the coming year, with the second half outperforming the first; demand is driven by data centre build-out, reshoring of advanced manufacturing, digital infrastructure and Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act funds.
- Europe construction equipment appears past its cyclical trough, with the first signs of recovery in the last quarter; modest, genuine growth is expected in the year ahead, underpinned by infrastructure-led public investment, fiscal stimulus and energy transition projects.
- Small agriculture: North America is entering a recovery phase as farmers return to replacement cycles, with industry estimates of about five per cent growth; Europe is stabilising, with recovery expected to gather pace in the second half; India tractor demand has been stable. Management expects healthy growth in small agriculture.
- Large agriculture is still in a cyclical downturn: North American large tractor volumes are declining in the mid-to-high teens year on year, industry volumes are expected to fall a further fifteen to twenty per cent, and recovery will be gradual. Europe shows more encouraging signals.
- The aftermarket gives stable revenue in North America and Europe, largely insulated from swings in the original equipment cycle.
- West Asia tensions in March 2026 disrupted supply chains; the resulting rise in input costs was partly offset by favourable currency movements.
- Trailing twelve-month new business wins have crossed ₹225 crore (printed as 'H225 crore') and grew by more than twelve and a half per cent quarter on quarter; the wins are spread across several business lines and markets.
- In the small agriculture customer base, inventory replenishment is gaining momentum and order books continue to strengthen.
- New programme wins in Europe and participation across multiple tractor platforms position the company for the eventual recovery in large agriculture.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Paid interim dividend of Rs.37.7cr and special dividend of Rs.101.55cr (Rs.22.50/share); net cash position of Rs.226cr; inorganic growth remains strategic priority, no constraint due to strong balance sheet

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Uniparts expands capacity through a modular model. It adds balancing equipment instead of building large greenfield plants and says it has enough manufacturing headroom to take on new business without significant upfront capital. Growth capex has been kept at 2.5-3.5% of revenue and goes to productivity, process optimisation and selective capacity additions. Utilisation is monitored plant by plant to remove bottlenecks. The footprint is seven manufacturing facilities (six in India, one in the US), with warehouses in the US, Europe and Mexico. In FY2025-26 the Company introduced lights-out manufacturing at its US facility and brought a critical manufacturing process in-house there. Surface finishing facilities are being upgraded at selected plants. The Farmparts facility in Ludhiana and the Vizag facility won industry cluster awards.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and strategic; emphasizes operational resilience, dual-shore advantage, disciplined capital allocation, and inorganic growth pipeline; tone is upbeat on construction and European Ag, cautious on NA large Ag

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- scale: Largest global share in tractor three point linkages and the lead position in precision machined parts for construction, forestry and mining equipment — evidence: the AR says it holds the top share of the global three point linkage market and leads the worldwide CFM precision machined parts space, with shares of 16.68% and 5.92% as of fiscal 2022 (the share figures are four years old)
- customer lock-in: Long-standing supplier to the largest OHV OEMs — evidence: it supplies all of the world's top ten off-highway vehicle manufacturers in agriculture and half of the top ten in construction (outside China), forestry and mining, and its top three customers have been with the Company for more than fifteen years
- distribution: Warehouse-led delivery close to customers in its export markets — evidence: three warehouses (two in the US, one in Germany), and 51% of FY2025-26 revenue came from warehousing sales (26% direct exports, 23% local deliveries)
- integration: Vertically integrated dual-shore manufacturing — evidence: six plants in India and one in the United States, each equipped for forging, machining, heat treatment, welding, surface finishing, prototyping and testing

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: North American large Ag continued softness; global economic slowdown; geopolitical tensions; tariff volatility; rupee appreciation reversing FX benefits

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Mexico warehouse commissioning (Oct 2025) is a hidden catalyst for tariff mitigation and customer retention; 25% flat tariff on tractor parts (Oct 31) is a positive inflection for US aftermarket, not yet priced in

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Three priority growth areas: large agriculture, construction and small to mid-size fabrication, chosen because they fit long-term market opportunities and existing manufacturing capabilities.
- Scale the Ludhiana fabrication facility, which currently contributes about one per cent of revenue and is expected to rise as order conversion improves.
- Inorganic growth: actively evaluating acquisitions in large fabrication, hydraulic and power take-off segments to broaden the portfolio, deepen customer relationships and expand markets, with stated capital-allocation discipline.
- After the US tariffs on …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Order book] 'Our trailing twelve-month new business order book remains robust at over INR 225 crore, with a healthy pipeline. These wins span segments and geographies... The new business momentum is structural, and we intend to build on it.'
- [Customer concentration] The concentration chart reads top customer 28% / 27% / 31%, top 5 customers 61% / 64% / 71%, top 10 customers 76% / 78% / 84% across FY25 / FY26 / Q1FY27 - i.e. concentration stepping up in Q1FY27.
- [End markets] Construction equipment momentum from H2 CY2025 continues, supported by US technology-investment-led and European government-led infrastructure spending; large agriculture 'remains subdued', with leading OEMs indicating 'CY2026 represents the cyclical bottom, with a more meaningful recovery expected through CY2027'; western small ag is turning after 'three consecutive years of volume declines'.
- [Tariffs] 'Tariff-driven price volatility has led to some demand skewing, as higher prices caused customers and channel partners to moderate their purchasing. With tariffs having since come down, we expect this to normalise and the segment to return to growth.'
- [Certification] Milestones cite '3 units SER certified by Caterpillar' (2024) and 'Two factories SER certified by Caterpiller second year in a row' (2025); the covering exchange letter describes the company as 'An ISO 9001:2008 & 14001:2004 Company'.
- [Group structure] Uniparts India Ltd. sits above Gripwel Fasteners Pvt. Ltd. (GFPL), Gripwel Conag Pvt. Ltd. (GCPL), Uniparts USA Ltd. (UUL), Uniparts India GmbH (UIG) and Uniparts Olsen Inc (UOI); only two 100% holdings are marked and the extract does not bind them to specific entities.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
